applyTo: "**/*_test.go"

# Test fixtures in codeql-abom

## Never hand-write CodeQL output

BQRS and SARIF fixtures must be produced by the CodeQL CLI and checked into `testdata/`. Never
construct them in Go, and never hand-edit a checked-in one.

Hand-written BQRS looks right, compiles, and lies. A fake that emitted `startLine = 1` for every
tuple collapsed every edge into one row, because `normalize.EdgeKey` includes source location
and `abom_edge` upserts on `edge_key`. The symptom was a discovered dependency missing from
`abom_frontier`, and several rounds went into hunting a phantom bug in `frontier.Enqueue`, which
was correct all along.

Regenerate from the checked-in source tree instead:

```bash
codeql database create --language=actions \
    --source-root=ql/actions/abom/test/AbomEdges /tmp/abom-fixture-db
codeql query run --database=/tmp/abom-fixture-db --output=/tmp/edges.bqrs \
    ql/actions/abom/src/AbomEdges.ql
codeql bqrs decode --format=json --output=internal/<pkg>/testdata/abom-edges.json /tmp/edges.bqrs
```

If a test needs different data, change the **fixture source tree** and regenerate. Put the
regeneration command in a comment above the fixture constant.

A corollary worth checking: any fixture whose tuples share a location or other identity field is
not exercising the identity logic at all.

Real fixtures also earn tests you would not have thought to write. The real `abom-edges.json`
contains `docker://alpine:3.20` and `actions/checkout` at two different refs, which produced
`TestExpandDoesNotQueueUncloneableTargets` and `TestExpandQueuesAnActionOnceAcrossRefs`.

## When a test fails on data shape, suspect the fixture first

Hand-built graph fixtures drift from what ingestion actually produces. This has caused three
separate false alarms:

| Fixture omitted | Real ingestion sets | Broke |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Owner`/`Repo` on external nodes | both, always | advisory matching (`owner \|\| '/' \|\| repo`) |
| workflow nodes entirely | one per workflow file | workflow-level finding linkage |
| `Path` on workflow nodes | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | finding-to-node fallback |

Check the real database before changing any code:

```bash
sqlite3 /tmp/abom-real/abom.db "SELECT node_key, node_kind, path, owner, repo FROM abom_node LIMIT 5;"
```

Then make the fixture match reality, and expect node-count assertions to need updating.

## Naming and comments

Name tests after the behaviour they protect, not the function they call. Put the *reason* the
behaviour matters in a comment above the test — that is what tells a future reader whether a
failure is a regression or an intentional change.

```go
// A retracted advisory must not be reported: its own publisher no longer stands behind it.
func TestWithdrawnAdvisoriesAreNotReported(t *testing.T) {
```

## Surface failures, do not swallow them

Worker-pool jobs fail silently by default, which hides a consume-phase error behind an
unrelated-looking assertion. Wire `OnEvent` in test harnesses:

```go
OnEvent: func(ev work.Event) {
    if ev.Kind == work.EventFailed {
        t.Logf("job %s failed: %v", ev.Job.Repository, ev.Err)
    }
},
```

## Guard the invariants

Some tests exist to stop the architecture eroding rather than to test a function. Do not delete
or weaken them without saying why: `TestSchemaHasNoVerdictColumns`,
`TestCommonalityStillOutranksYieldPreference`, `TestSeedRepositoryIsNotDemotedToUpstream`,
`TestRemediationScoreIsSeverityTimesReachOnly`, `TestUpstreamRepositoriesStillContributeTransitiveEdges`.
